This page provides a comprehensive overview of two key physics concepts: efficiency and payback time, presented under the heading "P1b: Efficiency and Payback Time." It defines efficiency as the ratio of useful energy output to total energy input, illustrated with an example of a coal fire being 25% efficient. The page also explains payback time as the duration required to recoup an initial investment through savings, using wall cavity insulation as an example where a £400 cost results in a 5-year payback period due to £80 in annual savings. Both concepts are accompanied by their respective formulas, which can be manipulated for different calculations.

- Efficiency is defined as the amount of energy turned into useful energy.

- Wall cavities have a cost of £400 and save £80 per year, resulting in a 5-year payback time.

- The formula for payback time is: Payback Time = Cost / Savings.
